Riverside, San Pedro, Laguna Dear Sangguniang Barangay Member Iwasaki: This refers to your letter dated December 28, 2021 requesting for this Department's legal opinion conceming the propriety of using the Barangay Development Fund to subsidize the monthly amortization of the informal settlers in your barangay. At the outset, we note your observation that pursuant to DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2017-1, allotment from the development fund for the purchase and development of land for the purpose of relocating informal settlers is allowed. As represented in your letter, about 300 out of 685 households of Barangay Riverside, San Pedro, Laguna, are considered informal settlers. Accordingly, these households are currently undergoing the Community Mortgage Program. Apparently, the Social Housing Finance Corporation are asking the aforesaid informal settlers to pay monthly installment basis. Thusly, you proposed to the Barangay Development Council the inclusion of funds in the Barangay Development Fund to subsidize the monthly amortization of the informal settlers thereat to expedite the processes so they may own the lot where their houses are located. However, there are reservations from among the members of the Sangguniang Barangay insofar as the legality or validity of such proposal is concemed. Hence, your query. At the outset, may we note that the guidelines on the appropriation and utilization of the twenty percent (20%) of the annual internal revenue allotment (IRA) for development projects has been recently revised and circularized thru Joint Memorandum issued by this Department, the Department of Budget and Management, and the Department of Finance, entitled "Revised Guidelines on the Appropriation and Utilization of the Twenty Percent (20%) of the Annual Intemal Revenue Allotment for Development Projects (DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1 series of 2020, dated 2 November 2020). Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

It is worthy to note that the aforesaid Guidelines, albeit it specifically enumerates items that are not to be funded in the 20% Development Fund (DF), the same did not specifically provide for the items that may be allowed to be charged against the 20% DF. Nevertheless, Item 3.2.1 of the aforesaid JMC expressly provides that [t]he 20% DF shall be utilized to finance the LGUs' priority development projects, as embodied in their respective duly approved local development plans, and medium-tenn and annual investment programs, which should be harmonized with the Regional Development Plan and the Philippine Development Plan. Further, Item 3.2.2 thereof provides that [tlhe development projects that may be included under the 20% DF shall be those that are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to emcient and effective local govemance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare of the people. Relatedly, Republic Act No. 7270 otherwise known as the Urban Development Housing Act of 1992 mandates local govemment units (LGU) to undertake the provision of housing services for their respective constituents. Hence, LGUs play an important role in the provision of decent housing for low-income families. Accordingly, this Department is of the view that the proposal to fund the amortization of informal settlers appears to be within the purview of Item 3.2.2, as above-stated. Moreover, the DBM, in its letter dated 4 March 2021, has settled that it is the LGUs concemed that are in a better position to determine the programs, projects and activities (PPAs) and expenses that may be charged against their respective 20% development funds (DFs), as long as the same do not fall within the purview of the list of expenditure items not allowed to be charged against DF as enumerated in item 3.2.5 of DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 1. In view of the foregoing, this Department opines that the said proposal may be allowed to be charged against the 20% DF. Let it be emphasized, however, that the same should be subject to budgetary limitations under Section 324 of the Local Government Code. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Ve ly yours, BY AUT ITY OF THE MARTIN B. DINO CRETARY: Undersecretary for Barangay Affairs Dir. ARIEL O. IGLESIA CESO IV Regional Director, DILG-CALABARZON 3F Andenson Bldg. 1, National Highway Brgy.
